classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the supplied counter groups as two signed products and cancel positive–negative pairs to find the remaining signed total.

content.prompt: Use the counters to work out $2 \times 5 + 3 \times (-4)$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4, counter groups beneath the prompt
spec.description: Ten positive counters on the left in two rows of five; twelve negative counters on the right in three rows of four. Both groups start at the same vertical position.
spec.mathematics: The positive counters represent 2 × 5 = 10. The negative counters represent 3 × (−4) = −12. Ten zero pairs leave two negative counters.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied counters and their unit labels remain visible. Cancellation marks and the final answer are not included in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
$$
\begin{align*}2\times5+3\times(-4)&=10+3\times(-4)\\&=10+(-12)\\&=-2\end{align*}
$$
Pair each of the 10 positive counters with a negative counter. Each pair makes zero, leaving 2 negative counters.
